newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH sales up in 1996, DFS buy to hit EPS in 1997.
newsitem.headline: LVMH sales up in 1996, DFS buy to hit EPS in 1997.

text.p: French luxury goods conglomerate LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Thursday that its $2.6 billion acquisition of U.S. duty free chain DFS would weigh on earnings per share for 1997.

But the group is targetting higher sales and profits this year before the impact of the acquisition, LVMH said in a statement announcing a 4.6 percent rise in provisional 1996 sales to 31.14 billion francs. It said 1996 sales rose in the champagne and wines and designer leather goods divisions, but fell for cognac and spirits and perfumes and beauty products.

"The objective set for LVMH in 1997 is for a new increase in sales and profits before the impact of the DFS acquisition," the statement said. "The acquisition should lead to growth on the order of 50 percent for sales and close to 30 percent for LVMH's operating profit."
But the acquisition would be dilutive. An LVMH spokeswoman said it would mean lower earnings per share in 1997.

LVMH bought 61.25 percent of DFS for $2.6 billion last year. It is expected to report its 1996 results on March 20. It posted a 5.4 percent rise in 1996 first-half net attributable profit in September and said then it expected an rise in full-year profit.
